note: Requests and the catalogue items that should be returned for each, over the 123 published items of examples/29_intelligence_service/starter-catalogue on 21 September 2026. The first group of 105 is taken unchanged from that catalogue's own search-queries.json, which records one expected item for each query and who wrote it. That file and the catalogue's REVIEW.md state that the item purposes were given the words those queries used until every one passed, so the group is a smoke check and not independent evidence; it is kept here and reported separately for exactly that reason. The second group of 249 was written for this measurement from each item's title and declared tags, in the words a customer's coding tool would send, before any ranking was measured against them, and it was not revised afterwards. Every catalogue item is expected by at least one request. A request with an empty relevant list is one this catalogue cannot answer, kept so that a confident wrong answer is visible rather than invisible.

authors.starter_catalogue_author: the author of the item purposes, recorded in search-queries.json
authors.starter_catalogue_reviewer: an adversarial reviewer who wrote queries after the purposes existed, recorded in search-queries.json
authors.search_quality_session: the engineering session of 2026-09-21 that built this measurement; it wrote no item purpose and changed no catalogue item

split_rule.held_back_when: the first eight hexadecimal characters of the SHA-256 digest of the query text, read as a base sixteen number, leave no remainder when divided by four
split_rule.why: the split follows from the query text, so no result can move a query between the two groups
